citations.narrative:
On review of the IACUC meeting minutes of 6-18-2025, it was found that “One sheep escaped her enclosure and injured
herself, she has been treated and is under observation until she heals before she is returned to the farm.” On questioning
the attending veterinarian about the injury, she stated that the sheep did not escape her enclosure but was startled at
feeding time on the morning of May 26, 2025, and jumped backwards catching her left shoulder on an exposed bolt that
caused a 20-inch laceration. The wound was immediately surgically repaired. She was moved to an indoor enclosure to
stay until suture removal. The day after her sutures were removed on June 4, 2025, she was moved back to an outdoor
enclosure.
On review of the daily observation notes for this same Columbia/Rambouillet cross ewe, she was found to have a new 10-
inch laceration over her left shoulder the morning of June 12, 2025, that was also repaired the same day. The facility
personnel said that they could not locate what object caused the second laceration as there was no obvious physical
trace found.
Inspection of the largest outdoor enclosure by the inspector on July 22, 2026, revealed two nail heads slightly protruding
from a perimeter wood wall and a couple of fence wires that had exposed points in two of the seven smaller outdoor
enclosures. Inspection of the three indoor enclosures revealed the pens were assembled with the screw ends facing
inward, toward the animal(s) instead of facing outward, away from contained animals. There was a metal feed container
with sharp edges in one of the indoor enclosures.
The laceration wounds this ewe sustained demonstrate that the enclosure(s) did not protect her from injury.
The facility must be constructed of such material and of such strength as appropriate for the animals involved. The indoor
and outdoor housing facilities shall be structurally sound and shall be maintained in good repair to protect the animals
from injury and to contain the animals.
Correct by August 5, 2026
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with facility representatives.
